source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Andrea was born with a cleft lip and palate. The lip was repaired at 3 months, and the palate repair is planned later.
questions.stem: On the first day after the cleft lip repair, how should the nurse care for the incision?
options: Rinse it with sterile water after feedings
Clean it only when exudate forms
Rub it gently to remove crusts
Remove the Logan bar to clean it
questions.rationale: The incision is rinsed with sterile water after every feeding and patted dry, never rubbed. The Logan bar protects the suture line and stays in place.
explanations: Cleaning is routine, not only when exudate forms.
Removing it adds tension to the incision.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q144 (PDF p. 294)
questions.quote: The incision should be rinsed with sterile water after every feeding.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Baby Andrea was born with a cleft lip and palate. The lip was repaired at 3 months, and the palate repair is planned later.
questions.stem: Years later, at a preschool checkup after her palate repair, which question BEST screens for a long-term complication?
options: 'Does she play with an imaginary friend?'
'Does she sometimes not respond when called?'
'Does she still eat soft food only?'
questions.rationale: Children with cleft palate get frequent otitis media, which can lead to hearing loss. Not responding may mean she cannot hear well. Imaginary friends are normal at this age.
explanations: Unrelated to cleft palate after repair.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q44 (PDF p. 183)
questions.quote: A child with cleft palate is at risk for developing frequent otitis media, which can result in hearing loss.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After spinal rod insertion for scoliosis, which assessment is MOST important in the immediate postoperative period?
questions.rationale: Spinal manipulation can impair neurovascular status, so circulation, sensation, and motion are checked at least every 2 hours. Pain and urine output matter but come second.
explanations: Correct: neurovascular checks are the priority.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q58 (PDF p. 199)
questions.quote: neurovascular checks, including circulation, sensation, and motion, should be done at least every 2 hours.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 2-year-old has just had a hip spica cast applied. Which action BEST protects the child's skin?
options: Change the diaper at least every 2 hours
Leave the genital area open to air
Check the skin only once a day
questions.rationale: The spica cast leaves the genital area open. Diapers are changed at least every 2 hours by day (3 to 4 hours at night) so urine and stool do not soil the cast and damage the skin.
explanations: Correct: frequent changes protect skin and cast.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q61 (PDF p. 206)
questions.quote: diapers will be in use and will need to be changed at least every 2 hours during the day

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with decorticate posturing suddenly shows decerebrate posturing. How should the nurse interpret this?
questions.rationale: A change from decorticate (flexor) to decerebrate (extensor) posturing usually means neurologic function is deteriorating, and the provider is notified.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q84 (PDF p. 230)
questions.quote: The progression from decorticate to decerebrate posturing usually indicates deteriorating neurological function

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 3-year-old admitted with croup has a respiratory rate of 28. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: A normal respiratory rate for a 3-year-old is about 20 to 30 breaths per minute, so the nurse documents it. Nasal flaring, retractions, and stridor would signal distress.
explanations: Not needed for a normal rate.
Correct: the rate is normal for the age.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q86 (PDF p. 232)
questions.quote: The normal respiratory rate for a 3-year-old child is approximately 20 to 30 breaths per minute.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which food or drink is BEST to offer a child after tonsillectomy?
questions.rationale: Clear, cool liquids are best. Citrus, carbonated, and very hot or cold drinks irritate the throat. Milk coats the throat and causes throat clearing, which can cause bleeding. Red liquids look like blood.
explanations: Correct: clear, cool, and not red.
Red color can be mistaken for blood.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q106 (PDF p. 255)
questions.quote: Red liquids need to be avoided because they give the appearance of blood

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant is HIV-positive. Which home-care action BEST reduces the infant's risk of complications?
options: Check the fontanel daily for bulging
Feed only in an upright position
questions.rationale: Meticulous skin care protects an HIV-infected infant from secondary infections. The other actions are unrelated to HIV.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q112 (PDF p. 261)
questions.quote: Meticulous skin care helps protect the HIV-infected infant from secondary infections.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of Individuals: Communicable & Non-Communicable Diseases
questions.stem: What is the MOST common complication of mumps?
options: Orchitis with a red, swollen testicle
questions.rationale: Aseptic meningitis is the most common complication of mumps (nuchal rigidity, lethargy, vomiting). Mumps can cause one-sided deafness, but this is uncommon.
explanations: It occurs, but is not the most common.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q115 (PDF p. 265)
questions.quote: The most common complication of mumps is aseptic meningitis

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement about brain tumors in children younger than 3 years is accurate?
options: Radiation is the treatment of choice
Headache and vomiting are the classic symptoms
The head is never shaved before surgery
questions.rationale: Headache and vomiting are classic. Total surgical removal is the treatment of choice. Radiation is avoided under age 3 because of its toxic effects on the developing brain.
explanations: Radiation is avoided at this age.
Only as much hair as needed is shaved.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q117 (PDF p. 267)
questions.quote: Radiation therapy is avoided in children younger than 3 years because of the toxic side effects on the developing brain

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Parents of a child with viral pneumonia ask about treatment. Which statement shows they need MORE teaching?
questions.rationale: Treatment of viral pneumonia is supportive: oxygen, chest physiotherapy, and IV fluids. Antibiotics are not given unless the pneumonia is bacterial.
explanations: Correct answer: antibiotics do not treat viruses.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q118 (PDF p. 268)
questions.quote: Antibiotics are not given unless the pneumonia is bacterial.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Nurse Bea plans a tepid tub bath for 4-year-old Kiko, who has a temperature of 39.6°C.
questions.stem: How should Nurse Bea prepare the bath?
options: Add rubbing alcohol to the water
Start warm and add cool water gradually
questions.rationale: Adding cool water to a warm bath lowers the temperature gradually, so the child adjusts without chilling. Alcohol is toxic and causes vasoconstriction. The bath lasts 20 to 30 minutes.
explanations: Too short; 20 to 30 minutes is needed.
Cold water causes shivering, which raises heat production.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q143 (PDF p. 293)
questions.quote: Adding cool water to an already warm bath allows the water temperature to slowly drop.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Nurse Bea plans a tepid tub bath for 4-year-old Kiko, who has a temperature of 39.6°C.
questions.stem: What should Nurse Bea do right after the bath?
options: Dress Kiko in a light cotton shirt
Cover Kiko with a heavy blanket
questions.rationale: Light cotton keeps the child from chilling. Blankets raise body temperature, and the temperature is rechecked about 30 minutes after the bath.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q345 (PDF p. 513)
questions.quote: Cotton is a lightweight material that will protect the child from becoming chilled after the bath.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: After surgical closure of a meningomyelocele, how should the infant be positioned?
options: Supine with a binder over the dressing
questions.rationale: The prone position keeps pressure off the surgical site on the back. The nurse watches closely for CSF leakage.
explanations: Supine puts pressure on the site.
Correct: prone protects the operative site.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q155 (PDF p. 305)
questions.quote: The prone position is maintained after surgical closure to decrease the pressure on the surgical site on the back

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has Reye's syndrome. Which complication should the nurse monitor for MOST closely?
questions.rationale: Reye's syndrome is an acute encephalopathy after a viral illness, with cerebral edema and fatty liver changes. Increased ICP is a major problem, and hypoglycemia (not hyperglycemia) occurs.
explanations: It follows viral, not bacterial, illness.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q162 (PDF p. 313)
questions.quote: Intracranial pressure and encephalopathy are major problems associated with Reye’s syndrome.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Jun-jun, 8, is admitted with suspected rheumatic fever three weeks after an untreated sore throat.
questions.stem: Which laboratory result BEST supports the diagnosis?
questions.rationale: An elevated antistreptolysin-O (ASO) titer shows a recent streptococcal infection and is the most reliable test supporting rheumatic fever. A high WBC count is not specific.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q173 (PDF p. 326)
questions.quote: The most reliable and best standardized test to confirm the diagnosis is the ASO titer.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Jun-jun, 8, is admitted with suspected rheumatic fever three weeks after an untreated sore throat.
questions.stem: Which finding is a MAJOR manifestation of rheumatic fever the nurse should prepare to manage?
options: Cool, pale skin over the joints
White, painful lesions on the trunk
Carditis with a new heart murmur
questions.rationale: Rheumatic fever is a delayed inflammatory reaction to group A beta-hemolytic streptococcal infection. Major manifestations include carditis (murmur, cardiac enlargement) and subcutaneous nodules over bony prominences.
explanations: Correct: carditis is a major manifestation.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q289 (PDF p. 448)
questions.quote: Major manifestations include carditis manifested as inflammation of the endocardium, including the valves

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A 5-year-old with tetralogy of Fallot has clubbed fingers. What does this finding reflect?
questions.rationale: Clubbing, a thickening and flattening of the fingertips, results from chronic tissue hypoxia and polycythemia.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q174 (PDF p. 327)
questions.quote: Clubbing, a thickening and flattening of the tips of the fingers and toes, is thought to occur because of chronic tissue hypoxia and polycythemia.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which stool characteristic does the nurse expect in a child with celiac disease?
questions.rationale: Gluten intolerance causes malabsorption, giving malodorous, pale, bulky, loose stools with excess flatus.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q210 (PDF p. 365)
questions.quote: The stools of a child with celiac disease are characteristically malodorous, pale, large (bulky), and soft (loose).

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding suggests an inguinal hernia in a child?
questions.rationale: An inguinal hernia appears as painless groin swelling when the child cries or strains. A dribbling stream suggests phimosis; absent testes suggest cryptorchidism.
explanations: Suggests partial obstruction of a herniated loop.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q214 (PDF p. 369)
questions.quote: Inguinal hernia is a common defect that may appear as a painless inguinal (groin) swelling when the child cries or strains.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which finding in a newborn supports a diagnosis of esophageal atresia?
questions.rationale: The esophagus ends in a blind pouch, so swallowed saliva cannot reach the stomach. It collects and flows out of the mouth, causing continuous drooling.
explanations: Correct: saliva cannot pass into the stomach.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q218 (PDF p. 373)
questions.quote: This condition prevents the passage of swallowed mucus and saliva into the stomach.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An infant has diarrhea. Which is an EARLY sign of dehydration?
options: Apical pulse of 200 beats per minute
questions.rationale: As fluid is lost, the pulse rises first to maintain circulation. Peripheral signs (cool, mottled skin and slow capillary refill) come later as circulatory failure develops.
explanations: A later sign of circulatory failure.
Correct: tachycardia is an early compensatory sign.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q346 (PDF p. 514)
questions.quote: The blood pressure will decrease and the pulse rate will increase. This will be followed by peripheral symptoms.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child has a new plaster cast on the arm. Which instruction helps the cast dry properly?
options: Lift the cast with the fingertips
Keep the cast covered with a blanket
Point a fan toward the cast
Keep the arm still in one position
questions.rationale: A fan speeds drying. The cast is lifted with the palms (fingertips leave dents), elevated on pillows, left uncovered, and repositioned every 2 to 4 hours. A dry cast sounds hollow.
explanations: Fingertips cause dents and pressure points.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q365 (PDF p. 533)
questions.quote: A fan may be directed toward the cast to facilitate drying.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which group of findings is typical of nephrotic syndrome in a child?
questions.rationale: Nephrotic syndrome causes edema, proteinuria, and hypoalbuminemia, with weight gain, anorexia, and abdominal pain. Blood pressure is usually normal or slightly low.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q367 (PDF p. 535)
questions.quote: Nephrotic syndrome refers to a kidney disorder characterized by edema, proteinuria, and hypoalbuminemia.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with intussusception passes a normal, formed brown stool. What should the nurse do?
options: Report it to the physician at once
questions.rationale: A normal brown stool usually means the intussusception has reduced itself. This is reported at once because the plan may change.
explanations: The finding needs to be reported.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q455 (PDF p. 635)
questions.quote: Passage of a normally formed brown stool usually indicates that the intussusception has reduced itself.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child with autism spectrum disorder will attend a day care center. What is the PRIORITY when planning the child's activities?
questions.rationale: A child with autism may not anticipate danger, may self-injure, and has sensory-perceptual deficits, so safety comes first.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q495 (PDF p. 688)
questions.quote: The child with autism is unable to anticipate danger, has a tendency for self-mutilation, and has sensory perceptual deficits.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Maya, 6, is admitted for tonic-clonic seizures. Nurse Gino is preparing her room and care plan.
questions.stem: Which items should Nurse Gino place at the bedside?
questions.rationale: Airway obstruction and increased oral secretions are the main complications during and after a seizure. Suction prevents choking, and oxygen prevents hypoxia.
explanations: Not routinely needed at the bedside.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q498 (PDF p. 691)
questions.quote: Suction is helpful to prevent choking and oxygen is helpful to prevent cyanosis.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.situation: Maya, 6, is admitted for tonic-clonic seizures. Nurse Gino is preparing her room and care plan.
questions.stem: Which planned intervention is UNSAFE for Maya?
options: Keep the bed in the low position
Restrain her limbs during a seizure
Pad the side rails of the bed
Turn her to her side during a seizure
questions.rationale: Restraints can injure a child during a seizure. The bed is kept low, side rails are padded, and the child is turned to the side so saliva drains out.
explanations: Correct answer: restraints can cause injury.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q496 (PDF p. 689)
questions.quote: Restraints (immobilization) are not to be applied to a child with a seizure because they could cause injury to the child.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: A child is admitted for removal of a malignant brain tumor. Which action ensures a safe environment?
options: Use a wheelchair for all activity
Assist with walking at all times
questions.rationale: Seizure precautions are used before and after surgery for any child with a brain tumor. Mobility aids are needed only if deficits exist.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q507 (PDF p. 702)
questions.quote: Seizure precautions should be implemented for any child with a brain tumor, both preoperatively and postoperatively.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: An adolescent with conjunctivitis wears contact lenses. Which instruction is MOST appropriate?
options: Get a new set of contact lenses
questions.rationale: A new set of lenses prevents reinfection. Eye makeup is replaced, not banned. Cool compresses ease pain, and isolation lasts 24 hours after starting antibiotics.
explanations: Makeup is replaced, not avoided forever.
Cool, not hot, compresses are used.
Isolation is needed for 24 hours on antibiotics.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q522 (PDF p. 717)
questions.quote: A new set of contact lenses should be obtained.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which home-care plan by a mother of a child with croup is CORRECT?
options: Give sips of warm fluids during an attack
questions.rationale: Warm fluids relax the vocal cords and thin mucus. Cough syrups and cold medicines dry and thicken secretions. A cool-mist humidifier is safer than a steam vaporizer.
explanations: Risk of burns; use cool mist.
Correct: warm fluids ease the attack.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q635 (PDF p. 853)
questions.quote: Sips of warm fluid will relax the vocal cords and thin the mucus.

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which discharge instruction is correct after a child's heart surgery?
options: Rub lotion and powder on the incision
Play outside every day after discharge
questions.rationale: A fever above 38°C (100.5°F) is reported. No lotions or powders go on the incision until it heals, outdoor play is restricted for several weeks, and school resumes about 3 weeks after discharge.
explanations: Nothing is applied until it is healed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q638 (PDF p. 856)
questions.quote: the primary health care provider must be notified if the child develops a fever of more than 100.5° F (38° C).

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Which statement by the parent of a 3-year-old with hemophilia shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll pad the corners of our tables.'
questions.rationale: Immunizations, dental hygiene, and routine well-child care are important in hemophilia. Supervision and a safe home environment prevent injury.
explanations: Correct answer: immunizations are still needed.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q650 (PDF p. 868)
questions.quote: The nurse must stress the importance of immunizations, dental hygiene, and routine well-child care.
